hypotheses.justification: Since R is Noetherian and N is finite, N is Noetherian. Thus `Module.Finite.of_injective f hf` recovers this instance, after which the existing proof applies unchanged. This includes zero modules and trivial rings.

Completion of a Noetherian ring is flat, so `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap f hf` proves the conclusion without finiteness of either module. `AlgebraTensorModule.coe_lTensor` identifies its underlying function with the displayed map. To avoid circularity with the subsequent `flat_of_isNoetherian` instance, retain the original finite-case proof as a helper, establish flatness using ideal inclusions exactly as that instance does, then prove the unrestricted result. Both finiteness hypotheses can therefore be removed together; zero modules, trivial rings, and all ideals are covered.
